subject: Clarify: no-training (training ban) scope, subprocessors & territorial coverage
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@medtechinc.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: legal@medtechinc.com
Date: Sun, 20 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify training ban & subprocessors (MedTech)

Tessa / Monica —

Thanks for the DPA draft. One open item from our side: we need an explicit, signed commitment that MedTech data (prompts + responses) will not be used to train models or improve underlying models ("no-training") by any Redwood subprocessor, in perpetuity or until we mutually agree otherwise.

Can you confirm the exact scope you can commit to and whether that commitment extends to:
- subcontractors (3rd-party inference providers, telemetry vendors)
- archives/backups and internal QA uses
- cross-border copies (EU-hosted data mirrored to US infra for DR)

Also: please provide your current subprocessor list (name, role, location) so our privacy team can validate. If you can attach a short feasibility note describing what evidence you can provide (logs, configs, deletion receipts), that would help speed approval.

Thanks — we want to get to signature next week if possible.

— Samir
Senior Privacy Counsel, MedTech Inc.

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@medtechinc.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify training ban & subprocessors (MedTech)

Samir —

Appreciate the clear ask. Short answer up front: we can commit to a no-training (no model improvement) covenant for customer-provided prompts and generated outputs for MedTech account(s) scoped in the DPA. That commitment covers Redwood and all downstream subprocessors that handle customer content as part of providing the Redwood service.

A few clarifying bullets and constraints so there are no surprises:
- Scope: customer prompts + model responses and any derived artifacts that are uniquely linked to MedTech input. It does not block Redwood from using anonymized, aggregated telemetry (e.g., router-level throughput stats, non-content model performance metrics) for service reliability.
- Subprocessors: we will include subprocessors in the DPA and certify they are contractually bound to the same no-training obligations by way of flow-downs.
- Backups/archives: copies that contain customer content will be covered by the no-training commitment; operational backups retained for DR are subject to standard retention policies and the same contractual limitation on model training.
- Cross-border DR: data mirrored for DR will be treated the same; if copies leave the designated geography they remain subject to the MedTech no-training restriction.

Attachments: I am attaching our current subprocessor CSV and a redlined DPA snippet with the proposed no-training clause. Monica has suggested stronger wording for the flow-down; she can comment formally.

Next steps: Monica / Aditya, can you confirm (1) legal wording and (2) what operational evidence we can provide (logs, deletion receipts, per-subprocessor attestations)? Samir — if this aligns with your ask I can circulate a final DPA amendment and DocuSign link.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: monica_patel@redwood.com <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, Samir Patel <samir@medtechinc.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify training ban & subprocessors (MedTech)

Folks —

Thanks Samir / Tessa. Draft legal position below, feel free to quote:

1) Contract language (proposed): "Provider and its subprocessors shall not use, access, process, or otherwise employ Customer Content (including prompts, completions, logs that can be reasonably attributed to Customer) to train or improve machine learning models, model weights, or model architectures, whether for Provider's internal products or third-party offerings. This prohibition shall apply for the duration of the Agreement and for a period of X years following termination, except where an explicit, documented consent from Customer is obtained."

2) Flow-downs / assurance: we will require subprocessors to execute flow-down agreements. For subprocessors unwilling to accept the clause we will provide an alternate plan (remove them from the processing path for MedTech workloads and replace with compliant vendors).

3) Evidence we can provide:
- Signed subprocessor addendum (or attestations) and a current CSV (attached).
- Operational attestations: periodic statements of compliance and signed SOC2 + customer-specific addendums where available.
- Technical evidence: requestable excerpts of access logs showing which nodes accessed customer content (retaining necessary redaction), and deletion receipts when requested. We can deliver hashed audit trails to avoid exposing full content.

4) Territorial transfers: where data must be mirrored for DR, transfers will be covered by the same contractual obligations. We will offer either (a) region-limited routing (keep primary and DR inside EU or US at Customer's choice) or (b) SCC/BCR-based transfer with encryption-at-rest and KMS access controls.

Operational note to Aditya: please prepare a short note (one-pager) describing what log extracts look like and the process for generating per-subprocessor attestations — Samir's team will want concrete samples.

Monica Patel
Lead Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com, Samir Patel <samir@medtechinc.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jul 2025 11:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify training ban & subprocessors (MedTech)

Quick technical rundown —

We can support the operational evidence Monica outlined. Practical details:
- Subprocessor list: attached CSV shows vendor, role, primary hosting region, and contact. We filter processing paths by customer tag; MedTech workloads can be pinned to a compliant processing pool.
- Logs: we can export access logs that include (timestamp, service, instance-id, action, subprocessor_id, content-pointer-id). We will hash content pointers so no PII leaves the export.
- Deletion receipts: when a delete request is issued, we record a job id and finalization timestamp; we can share the job id and signed confirmation. Full content is not included in the receipt.
- KMS & crypto controls: we can provide per-account KMS audit prints showing key usage (encrypted metadata only) and a diagram (attached) of how keys are separated by region.

Operational constraint: for complete end-to-end attestation per-subprocessor we will need a 7–10 business day window to collect signed confirmations from vendors. If MedTech needs faster turnaround we can provide interim attestations and hold signature contingent on final confirmations.

— Aditya
Senior Product Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir@medtechinc.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 24 Jul 2025 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify training ban & subprocessors (MedTech)

Team —

This is helpful, thank you. A few closing points from privacy:
- The proposed clause and flow-down approach are sufficient for MedTech's legal team provided the post-termination window is 3 years. Please add that to the redline.
- For evidence, hashed audit trails + deletion receipts are acceptable. We will request one vendor-level attestation for the highest-risk subprocessors (inference hosts and telemetry vendors).
- Regarding DR mirrors: we will pick region-limited routing (keep primary + DR in EU for our EU tenant). Please send routing options and the DocuSign link once the 3-year post-termination language is in the redline.

Action items:
- Monica: update the redline to include the 3-year post-termination period and re-circulate.
- Tessa: share DocuSign after redline revision.
- Aditya: prepare a sample hashed log extract and the vendor attestation template; expedite the 7–10 day vendor confirmations for the few high-risk subprocessors.

Assuming those arrive this week, we'll aim for signature early next week.

Best — Samir
Senior Privacy Counsel, MedTech Inc.
